events.title: Weather tracker: Why Europe’s wildfires are proving so fierce and difficult to stop
events.summary:
Wind and record-breaking heat are fuelling the continent’s explosive fire season, with Spain and France among worst hit

  • Explainer: what is a ‘fire cloud’, and how have they worsened wildfires in Europe?

  • Europe wildfires live – latest updates

A combination of an unusually wet winter, very low rainfall since spring and repeated record-breaking summer heatwaves is likely to explain why wildfires have ignited, spread and resisted control so readily across France and Spain in recent days.

About 90% of wildfires are started by human activity, typically igniting “fine fuels” such as vegetation grass, pine needles, litter and twigs. And recent weather has almost certainly made ignition far easier. Drought in western Europe has turned this vegetation – which normally dries after only a few hours of heat and low rainfall – into tinder.

events.title: Monday briefing: ​How the Cockroach ​protests ​have expose​d the ​cracks in ​India’s government
events.summary:
In today’s newsletter: Across ​the country, a ​younger generation is turning private disillusionment into public defiance​ against a government that once felt untouchable

Good morning. As flames engulfed parts of France and Spain this weekend, in India, the prime minister, Narendra Modi, was trying to put out a very different kind of fire. Thousands of people arrived in Delhi on Saturday to demand the resignation of his education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan. When he stepped down in the early afternoon, the protests turned into a triumphant block party.

But the Cockroach protests that have swept through India this summer are about much more than a single minister. They have humiliated Modi and undermined the indomitable power of his Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) that has ruled India for the past 12 years. They’re also a lesson in using humour to political advantage.

Wild fires | Authorities in France battled to contain a huge wildfire near Bordeaux in the south-west as Spain’s prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, warned Spain and the Iberian peninsula were suffering the effects of the climate emergency.

events.title: 'Trump Needs a Way Out of This War': Michel Yakovleff explains 'charade' over US-Iran negotiations
events.summary:
Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome General Michel Yakovleff, Professor at Sciences-Po and Former Vice-Chief of Staff at NATO's Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe (Shape).. He presents a strategic rather than tactical reading of the current lull in the US-Iran conflict. He argues that the apparent de-escalation is not evidence of diplomatic progress but of mounting structural constraints. Rather than viewing pauses in hostilities as signs of imminent peace, he frames them as consequences of political pressure, military logistics and industrial limitations.
 
At the centre of his argument is the proposition that modern warfare is ultimately governed by sustainability. Missile stockpiles, industrial production capacity, domestic political legitimacy and alliance commitments become as decisive as battlefield success. General Yakovleff contends that the United States retains ample military capability to continue operations against Iran in isolation, yet doing so progressively erodes its ability to deter other adversaries, reassure allies and sustain global commitments.

events.title: No basic services and nowhere to go: How Venezuelans are living a month after the earthquakes
events.summary: We visited the ruins of a housing complex built by the Chavista regime: the now homeless residents brave the heat, humidity, and flies from their tents, as they’re promised a house by 2027.

events.title: ‘Cockroach’ protests spread across India as leading activist ends hunger strike
events.summary: An activist has ended his 26-day hunger strike that galvanized India’s “Cockroach” protests, turning them into one of the biggest challenges to the government.

events.title: Oil prices surge to $100 per barrel after Red Sea attacks
events.summary: European and U.S. crude oil both jumped, hitting their highest levels in weeks.

events.title: Trump says Saudi Arabia must normalize Israel ties before nuclear deal is approved
events.summary: The president added that the deal “is totally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accords.”

events.title: U.S. signs landmark nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia
events.summary: The U.S. will support creating a civilian nuclear power program in the kingdom under the agreement, a senior administration official told NBC News.
